label: Title
notes: Open by locating the chapter in the curve half of the course and by naming the shift in viewpoint. Chapter 01 measured one curve at a time; this lecture studies controlled motion through curve space so length, bending energy, and constraints can be differentiated.

label: Route
notes: Use the route slide to give students a mental dependency graph. Families produce variation fields, variation fields produce first variation formulas, compact support turns those formulas into gradients, and gradients make the constrained elastica equation a linear algebra statement before it becomes an ODE.

label: One-Parameter Families
notes: Describe a family as a smooth surface traced by the parameters x and t, even when every t-slice is the curve of interest. The important computational point is that dot and prime are partial derivatives in two independent directions, so they commute before arclength enters.

label: Variation Fields
notes: Read the arrows along the base curve as the velocity of the curve family at t equals zero. Stress that a variation field is not a tangent vector in ambient space at one point; it is a whole vector-valued function along the entire curve.

label: Arclength Density
notes: Pause on the formula for the variation of ds because it is the local engine for everything that follows. Tangential stretching changes the speed immediately, while a purely normal displacement only affects length through how its derivative tilts relative to the tangent.

label: Commutator
notes: Emphasize the distinction between x-derivatives and arclength derivatives. Smooth partials commute, but d by ds contains the speed in its denominator, and the speed changes under variation. The commutator term is the bookkeeping cost of using moving geometric coordinates.

label: Length Gradient
notes: Use the integration by parts line to separate boundary behavior from interior geometry. When the variation is compactly supported, the endpoint term vanishes and the only possible obstruction to criticality is the curvature vector dT by ds in the interior.

label: Bending Density
notes: Frame bending energy as the length of the velocity of the tangent map on the sphere. The variation formula looks heavier because changing the curve changes both the tangent derivative and the arclength measure. The slide separates those roles before the integrations by parts.

label: Bulk Versus Boundary
notes: Move slowly through the boundary and bulk split. The boundary terms record what would have to be clamped for endpoint-sensitive variations. The bulk term is the gradient that remains visible to all compactly supported tests and therefore becomes the free elastica equation.

label: Fundamental Lemma
notes: Explain compact support as a microscope. If a smooth vector field pairs to zero against every small bump, then it cannot hide a nonzero value at any interior point. This is why variational identities turn into pointwise differential equations.

label: Critical Curves
notes: Connect the two Euler equations to geometric intuition. Length has a first-order-looking gradient and forces zero curvature, hence a straight segment. Bending has a third derivative of the tangent field, so its free critical curves are governed by a higher-order balance.

label: Constrained Criticality
notes: Present the Lagrange multiplier theorem as orthogonality, not as a mysterious optimization trick. If all length-preserving first variations also preserve bending to first order, then the bending gradient must lie in the one-dimensional span of the length gradient.

label: Torsion-Free Elastica
notes: The fixed-length wire problem adds the tension term to the free bending equation. Point out that the parameter lambda is global rather than a function of s; it records the single scalar constraint, and changing its value selects different elastic shapes.

label: Pendulum Correspondence
notes: Translate the elastica equation into motion of the unit tangent on the sphere. The curve itself is recovered by integrating T, so the pendulum path controls the direction of travel while the arclength parameter supplies the clock.

label: Planar Reading
notes: For planar elastica, the tangent lives on a circle, so the pendulum picture becomes especially concrete. Different tangent angle oscillations produce different reconstructed curves; the diagram is meant as a reading guide for the next chapter rather than a catalog of solutions.

label: Recap
notes: Close by tying the lecture back to the notebook checks. Students should leave with three reusable habits: represent variations as fields along a curve, isolate boundary terms before applying compact support, and read constrained equilibria as gradient alignment.
